title: Code Reviewer runner registration, version 1
description: How a runner on a customer's own machine gets to the app (#854, R1a of the runner epic #852). A member of a workspace makes a registration token in the app (short lived, usable once, shown once). The runner exchanges it with POST /api/runners/v1/register for a credential of its own (`crc_` and 43 characters; the app keeps only a hash). From then on every call carries 'Authorization: Bearer <credential>'. PUT /api/runners/v1/self tells the app what the runner is now (its labels, the version of its base, its manifest and limits live on the machine, not in the app); POST /api/runners/v1/credential renews the credential (the previous one works until the new one is used once, so a lost answer does not lock the runner out). A member can revoke a runner in the app: its next call is 401 RUNNER_UNAUTHORIZED. Every call updates `last seen`. A runner whose base is older than the minimum the app requires gets no job and the error 426 RUNNER_UPDATE_NEEDED. Errors are the ErrorResponse of contracts/runner-api.v1.json. A reader ignores fields it does not know; a writer sends only the fields below.

RegistrationToken.description: Made in the app by a member of the workspace; valid for one hour, usable once. Secret: never log it.

RunnerCredential.description: The runner's own credential. Secret: never log it.

BaseVersion.description: The version of the base every runner provides (the pinned OpenCode, the model door, the cost ledger, the finish tool, the git rules): three numbers and an optional pre-release tag. A pre-release is older than its release.

DeliveryUrl.description: Where the app sends the doorbell (`POST <url>`; the stop call goes to the same address with its last path segment `dispatch` replaced by `stop`, as in contracts/dispatch-webhook.v1.json). https without credentials; plain http only to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (the fakes and local development). An address that names a private, loopback, link-local or otherwise internal host is refused, and no redirect is followed.

DeliveryKeyId.description: Names the signing secret in `X-Dispatch-Key-Id`. Made by the app with the secret.

DeliverySecret.description: The signing secret of one dispatcher (`crw_` and 43 characters), minted by the app and shown once, in the answer that minted it and nowhere else (the app keeps it encrypted). It signs the doorbell and the stop call of this dispatcher only: a request signed with another dispatcher's secret is refused by the receiver. Secret: never log it.

DeliveryAnnouncement.description: How the dispatcher wants to learn of a job (#972). `poll` (the default, also when `delivery` is left out): it calls POST /claim itself and the app never rings it. `webhook`: the app sends the signed doorbell (a wake-up call without job data) to `url`, to every webhook dispatcher that matches the job's labels, when a job is enqueued and again when a job of its label group ends; the dispatcher then claims the next matching job (no `jobId` needed), and answers 200 ignored with the reason `busy` when it has no free slot. The first announcement of `webhook` makes the signing secret, and so does `rotateSecret: true`; announcing the same mode again keeps the secret that exists (it is never shown twice). Announcing `poll` drops the secret. `PUT /self` replaces what the app holds, so a dispatcher announces its delivery every time. The doorbell is sent only while the deployment runs the dispatch webhook (`RUNNER_DISPATCH=webhook`).

rotateSecret.description: Only with `webhook`: make a new secret now (the old one stops working at once).

DeliveryState.description: What the app holds of the delivery. `secret` is present only in the answer that minted it.

Label.description: A label a job can ask for. Lower case; the app lower-cases what it gets.

HarnessName.description: `opencode`, or `custom/name` for a harness the runner describes itself. Only OpenCode is in the platform's catalog; any other name exists for the app only while a runner announces it as ready.

ready.description: Installed, logged in and proven by the runner's self test. Only a ready harness is given a job.

RunnerManifest.description: What the runner adds to the base or overrides in the how. It never removes the base.

capabilities.description: For example `agent-docker`, announced only when the runner's self test ran a container in a Docker inside Sysbox.

RunnerLimits.description: What the runner works within, as it reports it. Informational: the limits are enforced on the machine.

RunnerAnnouncement.description: What a runner says about itself. The labels are all the routing reads (together with the ready harnesses and the version): a job runs on a runner that has every label it requires, which is every label its environment asks for. #971: the namespace `cr:` is reserved for the platform identity (`cr:managed`, `cr:size-<vCPUs>`). A runner on a customer's machine that announces such a label, in `POST /register` or in `PUT /self`, is refused with 422 `RUNNER_LABEL_RESERVED` of `contracts/runner-api.v1.json` (`fields` names each label by position, field code `reserved`) and nothing is stored; a body that is malformed in another way keeps its 400 `RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID`. The check is by identity, not by spelling: no runner credential is the platform. #972: `delivery` says how the dispatcher learns of a job (poll or webhook); a delivery that does not fit, or an address the app will not call, is 400 `RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID` with the field `delivery`, `delivery.mode`, `delivery.url` or `delivery.rotateSecret`.

RegisterRequest.description: POST /api/runners/v1/register. No other credential: the token is the proof. 401 RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN_INVALID when the token is unknown, used or expired (one answer for all three); 400 RUNNER_REQUEST_INVALID with `fields` for a body that does not fit.

name.description: The name in the list of runners: one line, 1 to 80 characters.

RegisterResponse.description: 201. The credential is in this answer and nowhere else.

minBaseVersion.description: The oldest base the app accepts, or null for none.

delivery.description: Left out for a runner that announced no webhook delivery.

AnnounceRequest.description: PUT /api/runners/v1/self: replaces what the app holds of the runner's labels, base version, manifest and limits. The runner sends it at start and whenever one of them changes.

updateNeeded.description: True when the announced base is older than the minimum: the runner gets no job until it is updated.

CredentialResponse.description: POST /api/runners/v1/credential: a new credential for the runner. The one it presented stays valid until the new one is used once.
